chunks: From him, from al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi', he said: Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Madaini narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him).
I said to him: 'May I be your ransom, I enter the mines and sell the gem with its dross using dinars and dirhams.' He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

I said: 'And I exchange dirhams for dirhams, and I turn the profit (ghillah) into clear (pure) [coin], and I turn the clear [coin] into profit.' He said: 'If there are dinars in it, there is no harm.'
He said: So I narrated that to Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said: 'Thus he said to me, his father.' Then he said to me: 'Where are the dinars?' I said: 'I do not know.'
Ammar said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'They are with the one who loses [value/weight].'

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمُ: Silver dirhams, the other currency type involved
key_terms.الدَّنَانِيرُ: Gold dinars, a specific currency type mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الغِلَّة: Profit or gain, often referring to the excess value or interest-like gain in exchange
key_terms.الوَضَح: Clear or pure coinage, distinguished from mixed or debased currency
key_terms.يَنْقُصُ: Loses or is deficient, referring to the party bearing the loss in the transaction

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling mixed gems and exchanging currencies with profit conversion in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith elucidates the Shia juristic principle of 'Riba al-Fadl' in currency exchange, distinguishing between pure gold/silver transactions and those involving mixed commodities like gems. The Imam clarifies that when dinars (gold) are part of the transaction, the strict requirement for immediate equal exchange is relaxed, allowing the party bearing the deficiency to retain the dinars, a nuance further confirmed by the scholarly commentary of Ammar ibn Musa.
